references.text: The women did not find Jesus' body when they entered the tomb: "But when they went in, they did not find the Lord Jesus' body" (Luke 24:3). This is the same event referred to in verse 23.
The angels' revelation at the tomb that the women report: "Two men in shining clothes stood before them" (Luke 24:4-5). Verse 23 refers to this vision of angels (ὀπτασίαν ἀγγέλων).
In Matthew's account, the angel at the tomb says that Jesus has risen and is no longer there (Matthew 28:5-6), which corresponds to the angels' message that Jesus is alive.
In Mark's account, the women meet a young man in white clothing who tells them that Jesus has risen (Mark 16:5-6), parallel to the vision of angels mentioned in Luke 24:23.
Mary Magdalene sees two angels in white sitting where Jesus' body had lain (John 20:12). This confirms the account of the vision of angels at the empty tomb.
Mary Magdalene reports that the Lord's body is missing from the tomb (John 20:2), which corresponds to the women not finding Jesus' body.
Angels (men in white clothes) who bring a message about Jesus' resurrection and ascension (Acts 1:10-11). The expression ὀπτασία ἀγγέλων (vision of angels) is found in similar themes.
Zechariah had seen a vision (ὀπτασία) in the temple (Luke 1:22). Luke uses the same word ὀπτασία for the vision of angels that the women experienced at the tomb.
The disciples later confirm that "the Lord has truly risen" (Luke 24:34). The angels' message that Jesus is alive (ζῆν) is confirmed.
Jesus declares himself: "I was dead, and see, I am alive" (Revelation 1:18). The angels' message in Luke 24:23 that Jesus is alive (ζῆν) finds its final confirmation here.
